acme-ops: Hey team — after our on-prem Private deploy went live yesterday, our app started returning intermittent 502s and TLS errors when calling the Redwood API. curl shows `tls: oversized record` and our container logs contain `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`. We suspect the corporate proxy. Any quick checks?

sara.support: Sorry you're hitting this. Quick questions: are you routing outbound through a TLS-inspecting proxy that re-signs certs? Which OS/container image? Do you have `HTTPS_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY` set?

acme-ops: Yes, BlueProxy 3.2 in front of everything. Containers are Debian 11 slim. We set `HTTPS_PROXY` in the service env. Not using NO_PROXY yet.

dan.infra: Okay. Two likely issues: (1) proxy is terminating TLS and presenting a different cert (needs proxy CA trusted in container), (2) proxy might be mangling SNI so backend sees wrong name. Can you run a quick curl to capture what cert the proxy presents?

acme-ops: Doing that now — command i'm running: `curl -v --proxy http://bp.company:3128 https://api.redwood.example/health` Output snippet:
```
* Connected to bp.company (10.10.2.4) port 3128 (#0)
* establish HTTP proxy tunnel to api.redwood.example:443
* CONNECT api.redwood.example:443 HTTP/1.1
> CONNECT api.redwood.example:443 HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established
* ALPN, server accepted to use h2
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.2 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS handshake, Server certificate (11)
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS alert, decrypt error (28)
* SSL: certificate subject: CN=BlueProxy-Intercept
* SSL: certificate issuer: CN=BlueProxy-Root
* curl: (35) error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure
```

acme-ops: The cert subject shows BlueProxy-Intercept, so proxy is MITMing. We tried `update-ca-certificates` in the image and added the proxy CA, but Java services still fail with `PKIX path building failed`.

sara.support: Java trusts the system keystore only if you update the JVM cacerts. For Java apps you need to import the proxy CA into the JVM `cacerts` with `keytool` or configure `javax.net.ssl.trustStore`. Example: `keytool -import -alias blueproxy -keystore $JAVA_HOME/lib/security/cacerts -file /etc/ssl/certs/blueproxy.pem` (password default is changeit).

kevin.runtime: Also double-check SNI passthrough on the proxy. If BlueProxy rewrites SNI or doesn't forward the original SNI host, backend will present the wrong cert or terminate early. Ask proxy admins to enable SNI passthrough for `api.redwood.example` or add an explicit passthrough rule for that hostname/port.

acme-ops: Good call — proxy team confirmed they are intercepting and rewriting SNI for TLS-inspected hosts. They want a temp workaround while they update rules.

dan.infra: Workarounds ordered by safety: (A) Add BlueProxy CA to system and JVM truststores (best if allowed), (B) Configure the service to use TLS passthrough by setting `HTTPS_PROXY`-exemptions for the Redwood endpoints (NO_PROXY), (C) Create an egress allowlist so traffic to Redwood control plane goes direct (bypass proxy) over the firewall.

acme-ops: How do we get a reliable list of domains/IPs to NO_PROXY/allowlist? We don't want to open too wide.

sara.support: We can give you our egress endpoints for Private customers. For control plane & API calls, allow outbound HTTPS to: `*.redwood-inference.com`, `api.redwood-inference.com`, and these CIDR blocks: `34.198.23.0/24`, `3.12.45.0/24`, `52.15.120.0/22` (please treat the CIDRs as example; we'll add exact list in the ticket). Ports: 443 (required). If you have strict egress rules, add SNI/pass-through for those hostnames instead of opening broad IP ranges.

deploy-bot: Created support ticket #SUP-2026-489 for this escalation and attached logs. Assigned to dan.infra.

kevin.runtime: Repro steps we recommend for your infra team:
1) From a dev host behind the proxy: `curl -v --proxy http://bp.company:3128 https://api.redwood.example/health` (captures proxy-presented cert info).
2) Extract the proxy cert: `echo | openssl s_client -connect bp.company:3128 -servername api.redwood.example 2>/dev/null | sed -n '/-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----/,/-----END CERTIFICATE-----/p' > /tmp/blueproxy.pem`
3) Add `/tmp/blueproxy.pem` to container OS trust and to JVM cacerts (if Java).
4) Test bypass: on a test host, `NO_PROXY=api.redwood.example curl -v https://api.redwood.example/health` — should connect and return 200.
5) If NO_PROXY works, put a narrow firewall rule to allow direct egress from your Redwood hosts to the listed hostnames/CIDRs on 443.

acme-ops: Will try steps 2-4. Quick Q: can we pin to a specific Redwood model endpoint port if needed? Our proxy team wants to know all destination ports.

sara.support: All standard APIs use 443. If you use dedicated or private control-plane tunneling we may include additional ports in the ticket; we'll confirm in #SUP-2026-489.

acme-ops: Thanks — extracted cert, added to system trust, and `curl --proxy` now shows the BlueProxy cert but `curl` returns 200. Java still failing, importing into cacerts now.

dan.infra: If after importing into `cacerts` Java still fails, check the JVM bundle in your container (sometimes Java is in a separate layer and not updated). Also ensure `javax.net.ssl.trustStore` env vars aren't pointing to a stale truststore.

acme-ops: Imported into cacerts, restarted services — all green. Will work with proxy team to enable SNI passthrough for Redwood hostnames and implement a narrow direct-e2e allowlist. Appreciate the quick help.

sara.support: Great — closing the immediate loop. We will keep SUP-2026-489 open until your proxy team confirms SNI passthrough or direct egress rules are in place. Ping us if you see any regression. :thumbsup:
